Then the Blessed One spoke the Vajra Secret of the entire assembly circle.
One should contemplate within the heart, upon the moon, the secret of all Tathāgatas, the *Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*, manifesting as a subtle vajra.
In this regard, listen to this secret empowerment of the *Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*:
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by nature; I am pure by nature.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the wisdom of emptiness.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of the vajra; I am pure by way of the vajra.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of yoga; I am pure by way of yoga.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of primordial wisdom; I am pure by way of primordial wisdom.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by commitment; I am pure by commitment.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the adamantine self whose essence is the passion for the emptiness of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the adamantine wisdom of the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), which is naturally pure as a Tathāgata.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of mantra; I am pure by way of mantra.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of wrath; I am pure by way of wrath.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of mind; I am pure by way of mind.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure in speech; I am pure in speech.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure in body; I am pure in body.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through the nectar of primordial wisdom; I am pure through the nectar of primordial wisdom.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through various commitments; I am pure through various commitments.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through the way of conduct; I am pure through the way of conduct.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through the three yogas; I am pure through the three yogas.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through consecration; I am pure through consecration.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure through worship; I am pure through worship.
Oṃ, I am of the nature of the vajra of the worship of all Tathāgatas.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the maṇḍala; I am pure as the maṇḍala.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the sovereign; I am pure as the sovereign.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the hero; I am pure as the hero.
Oṃ! All phenomena are pure as yoginīs; I am pure as a yoginī. Oṃ! All phenomena are pure in reality; I am pure in reality. He! All phenomena are free from causes; I am free from causes.
*Ru*: All phenomena are devoid of the syllable *ru*; I am devoid of the syllable *ru*.
*Ka*: All phenomena abide nowhere; I abide nowhere. *Oṃ*: All phenomena are instantly pure by nature; I am instantly pure by nature.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure in nature; I am pure in nature.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure in recitation; I am pure in recitation.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure in sustenance; I am pure in sustenance.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of being consumed; I am pure by way of being consumed.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of being non-concentrated; I am pure by way of being non-concentrated.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure by way of self-reflexive awareness; I am pure by way of self-reflexive awareness.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of hatred; I am pure of hatred.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of delusion; I am pure of delusion. Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of passion; I am pure of passion.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of pride; I am pure of pride.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of envy; I am pure of envy.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure of space-vajra; I am pure of space-vajra.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the three wheels; I am pure as the three wheels.
Oṃ, all phenomena are completely pure as the ḍākinīs; I am completely pure as the ḍākinīs.
Oṃ, all phenomena are completely pure as the six families; I am completely pure as the six families.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the Mother; I am pure as the Mother.
Oṃ, all phenomena are pure as the Seat; I am pure as the Seat.

In this manner, one should purify everywhere up to the cremation ground (*upaśmaśāna*). The purification of the three wheels consists of the twenty-four-fold Śiva,
which is liberated from time and occasion; it is the bond within the heart of the Yoginīs,
the supreme arising of Heruka for the sake of purifying the thirty-seven purifications.
The supreme and most excellent great secret, the Abhidhānottara.

The wise knower of reality who understands the counter-clockwise circumambulation for worship, the ritual placement (nyāsa), and the rightward circumambulation, should perform the placement of the five secret signs (chommā). One should not speak of this reality to anyone who has not been initiated.
For the teacher and the disciple who have been consecrated by the rite of bestowing the name, [the result is as described];
otherwise, that dull-witted fool, like a child, merely scratches himself with frost.
That fool falls into the terrifying hells such as Avīci.
A disciple who disregards the command of the book dies instantly, deluded by planetary influences,
fevers, poisons, diseases, and likewise by the afflictions of *ḍākinīs*,
by terrible obstacles, and by *vināyakas*; being thus slain, he shall go to hell.
Therefore, with every effort, the preceptor is to be served by the auspicious hands of the disciple;
thus, through the lineage of the succession of gurus, the practitioner of mantra attains accomplishment before long.
And one should preserve this Great Tantra, the sequence of the Abhidhānottara,
through the yoga of the divine yoginīs and with a mind of non-dual gnosis.
The supreme, eternal awakening in a single moment is surely attained [by avoiding]:
a human maiden, those of evil nature who disregard the command of the samaya,
one who is cruel, of cruel gaze, slain, extremely difficult to restrain, and likewise merciless.

A yogin should avoid such women who are difficult to please, envious, deceitful, treacherous, malicious, nihilistic, greedy, attached to others, and full of conceptual constructions; for they are far from spiritual accomplishment.

Furthermore, [he should choose] another woman, adorned with beauty and youth, who has practiced the single yoga, knows the ritual observances (*samaya*), and is firm in her vows; she should be free from shame,
devoid of desire, steadfast, without longing, and free from egoism.
The knower of mantras himself should practice the vow of knowledge together with her,
always wearing the five mudrās, having a skull as his crest-ornament,
carrying a skull-bowl and a khaṭvāṅga staff, and his body smeared with ashes.
Constantly eating human flesh, filled with the flowing stream of liquor,
and wearing a great cloak made from pieces of shrouds.
Satiated by the flow of blood, swarming with bees seeking leftovers,
and always accompanied by dogs, it remains in villages, gardens, and other such places.
One should always dwell in a cremation ground or at a marketplace;
one should not remain in a monastery frequented by Śrāvakas.
Enveloped by the darkness of ignorance, those who are incapable remain among the Śrāvakas in this world like destitute men among Bodhisattvas.
Performing the vajra-dance, one should always dwell in the cremation ground;
having eaten copiously of human flesh and drunk liquor together with one's beloved.
With a pure mind, one should meditate on the Heroic Leader upon the charcoal of a corpse;
or, in its absence, upon the Mahāmudrā, which is free from all distractions.
Likewise, she is born of primordial wisdom, the arising of the perfection of insight;
she is ungraspable, inexpressible, and established in the well-being of the non-dual form.
Having made the mind one-pointed and remaining engaged in meditative cultivation,
they achieve success through the stages of the methods of wisdom and skillful means, accompanied by blisses and joys.
One should meditate upon the Mahāmudrā, which is the direct realization of all phenomena;
being thus fully endowed with all views, one attains accomplishment in this very life.
The left-hand practice is wisdom, while the right-hand is likewise means;
endowed with the capacity for cultivation, one enjoys the Mistress of the Thirty-three.
When the yoginī Pūrvāsiddhi is attained, you shall enjoy a maiden named Yakṣiṇī,
as well as various other Gandharvīs, who are subject to the fivefold desires.
One should always meditate upon Āli and Kāli within the innermost secret of reality;
through the yoga of one's own chosen deity, one should conceptualize everything as one.

The Yogin should display the secret sign (*cchomma*) with his left hand; for this is the abode of heroes and the source of all secret signs. The entire world, the three realms with all its moving and unmoving beings, originates from the left.
Vajrasattva is praised in the *vālā* [ring finger], Vairocana resides in the *tarjanī* [forefinger],
Padmanarteśvara— the bestower of heroic accomplishment— is in the *dhārā* [middle finger],
the imperishable Ākāśatanu is in the *kaniṣṭhā* [pinky], and Hayagrīva is in the nails and fingernails.
The cause for the non-arising of the left-hand path among all heroes in their own abodes is as follows:

the messengers, being intensely eager, have made a firm resolve regarding the palms of the hands and the backs [of the hands]. Therefore, the practitioner must display the five secret signs (*cchommaka*).
Earth is known as Locanā; the water element is remembered as Māmakī;
Tārā and Pāṇḍaravāsinī are proclaimed as wind and fire;
and Cumbikā is likewise the perfection of emptiness.
In the midst of all the heroes, the wise one should ask for their abode and dismiss them;
this secret must not be disclosed, but kept hidden with great effort.
Thus, O hero, one should establish the *chomma* and then begin the sacrificial pap (*caru*) in one place.
The union of all heroes is the *Ḍākinījālasaṃvara*.
The Buddha has taught various secret signs (*cchommakā*) for beings who follow one another,
as well as the characteristics of the *ḍākinīs* and the characteristics of the female messengers (*dūtī*).
And all this has indeed been told for the benefit of practitioners:
the painting and the image, as well as the rules for their execution,
and the specific characteristics of the pigments by which practitioners attain success.

There are various beautiful mantras and diverse maṇḍalas; there is the delightful, divine commitment (samaya), and the various supreme yoginīs. Through this well-expounded method, one becomes a bestower of the yoginīs.
[He taught] the traditions of the ḍākinīs and various supreme families,
as well as the tradition of the guru’s festivals, desiring the welfare of his disciples;
he was one who knew the ritual procedures for lordship and was well-versed in the tantras of mantra.
The subsequent rites of the Abhidhāna are according to the sequence of rules of other tantras.
The mantra-practitioner should observe the animal and its various remaining species,
as well as the conduct of the Yoginīs and likewise the Ḍākinīs,
the Mātṛs, and the external mudrās born of the Vārāhī-kula.
The wise one should teach the conduct of all heroes and the practice of the wheel; he should observe the conduct of those who practice external yoga,
and he should instruct the beautiful and auspicious woman born of the lineage of Śrī Heruka.
One should learn the practice of conduct according to the specific customs of various regions;
one should learn conduct in detail from the Yoginītantras and the Yogatantras,
and through the sequence of the divisions of ritual action, attain mastery over all tantras.
The scriptures are the treatises on accomplishment, as well as the sūtras and birth stories;
they contain the practice for the unsurpassed state, the arising of the perfection of wisdom,
the thorough knowledge of external sciences, and the various supreme conducts.
One should place the steadfast state through yoga-meditation,
with a mind free from doubt regarding all food and activities;
for all mantras, firm realization is achieved by means of the hundred-syllabled mantra.
One should always recite the garland-mantra (mālāmantra), which accomplishes all desires and aims, by combining it with one's own name;
this is the *Yoginījālasamvara*, the most supreme even among the supreme.
The extraction of mantras, the armor, the heart and sub-heart,
the protection of the doors, the great yantra, the beautiful arrangement of the mandalas,
the placement of the script and mandala, and that which arises from the Saṃvīra-yoginī.
The supreme among all mantras, the most excellent of the Mother-letters (mātṛkā),
the secret of secrets, the beautiful compendium of all mantras,
the abode of all phenomena, the Mātṛkā from which the world arises.
One should not speak of this reality; otherwise, there will be a loss of accomplishment.
This is the supreme self, the unsurpassed accomplishment of desire.
By meditating upon it, one shall attain the state of the glorious Vajrasattva in this very life.
Clad in the armor of loving-kindness, armored with the shield of compassion,
and engaged in the cultivation of wisdom, they have utterly conquered the Māras of the afflictions.
[They possess] the great protection of the four-faced [mantra], which is marked by the vajra and responds to all challenges.

One shall desire the great protection of the wheel of command, which is triple-layered through the divisions of body, speech, and mind, marked with the vajra, providing supreme protection for the best of beings, bestowing all accomplishments,
and destroying the hosts of obstructors.
For this is the supreme protection for practitioners seeking awakening:
a vajra-fence of ritual stakes, a vajra-canopy upon the vajra-ground, a beautiful, wide-spreading awning that shields against the wicked Māras.
Neither Māra nor by Māra is one bound; rather, it is one's own mind that binds.
For him who has tamed his own mind, [Māra is no threat].
Having smeared [the ground] with cow dung and the like, one should draw a square.
For those whose bodies are like the axe and sandalwood, who abide in equanimity,
and for whom patience is as natural as the application of flowers— one should diligently bestow the supreme gift.
For the lamp that is pure by nature, the cultivation of incense is equanimity.
In the Abhidhānottara, the third chapter, concerning the Heart, Reality, and the Ultimate Meaning.
